advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider matching SEAM_INTERNAL_MODULES by package-qualified path rather than bare filename stem so the exemption is scoped to the reconciler seam.
evidence: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:666: `seam = _NO_SEAM if rel.stem in SEAM_INTERNAL_MODULES else _seam_bindings(tree)`
Header documents the per-FILE trust boundary but not that the match is name-only across the whole tree
advisory.finding: SEAM_INTERNAL_MODULES is matched by filename stem only (`rel.stem in SEAM_INTERNAL_MODULES`), so any file anywhere in src/ or scripts/ named git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, or _ref_lock_push.py is exempted from R3 regardless of directory/package, widening the trust boundary beyond the reconciler seam.
scenarios: A future unrelated module named git_adapter.py added elsewhere would silently be exempt from R3.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an R3 test that a `pkg.git_adapter.add(...)` (dotted-attribute receiver) composition outside the seam fires seam-composition.
evidence: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:465-473 handles `recv` as `ast.Attribute` with `name = recv.attr`, distinct from the `ast.Name` branch
Header comment claims support: `both ``git_adapter.add(…)`` and ``pkg.git_adapter.add(…)`` bind` (check_raw_git_writes.py `_seam_primitive` docstring)

search of tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py for `pkg.git_adapter` returns (no matches) — the Attribute-receiver branch is exercised by no test; all firing tests use a bare-name receiver (`git_adapter.add`), an alias (`ga.add`), a loader-bound name, or a bare from-import
advisory.finding: R3's dotted-attribute receiver branch (`pkg.git_adapter.add(...)`) is documented in the checker header and implemented as a distinct code path, but no test exercises it. A regression that broke the nested-attribute receiver resolution would pass the suite silently.
scenarios: A refactor of `_seam_primitive` that drops the `ast.Attribute` receiver branch would still pass every test
A caller importing the seam via a package handle (`import rebar_reconciler.git_adapter` then `rebar_reconciler.git_adapter.commit(...)`) is the exact case the branch targets and is unverified
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test mirroring test_r3_composed_add_commit_outside_seam_fires but with `import rebar_reconciler.git_adapter` and a call site `rebar_reconciler.git_adapter.commit(d, "m")`, asserting `_kinds(...) == ["seam-composition"]`.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm/adjust the bare-imported-primitive R3 path so a locally-shadowed primitive name does not spuriously fire (or narrow the 'over-binding is harmless' claim to the receiver path).
evidence: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:461: `if isinstance(func, ast.Name): return func.id if func.id in self.seam.primitives else None`
scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:302: `Over-binding a name is harmless — the primitive-name check still gates the emission`
`_seam_bindings` walks the whole module (ast.walk) and unions primitive names, so a from-import at module scope binds the bare name for every function even where it is locally rebound
dropped.finding: For a `from`-imported mutation primitive (bare-name path in `_seam_primitive`), module-wide binding means any bare call to that name fires as seam-composition even when the name has been locally reassigned/shadowed to an unrelated callable. The docstring claim 'Over-binding a name is harmless — the primitive-name check still gates the emission' only holds for the attribute-receiver path; on the bare-Name path (func.id in self.seam.primitives) there is no receiver gate, so a shadowed `add`/`commit` yields a false positive.
scenarios: A module does `from rebar_reconciler.git_adapter import add`, then in an unrelated function locally rebinds `add = list.append`-style helper and calls `add(...)` — R3 fires spuriously.
